claims.evidence: The witness report describes the item as a standing fan with visible branding and a control panel, consistent with a used household item.
The witness sees a display and buttons on the pole, which are common on rechargeable models, but no 'rechargeable' label or battery compartment was explicitly confirmed.

claims.claim: Lasts up to 2 hours when fully charged
claims.evidence: Battery runtime cannot be determined from static photos.
Variable speed battery performance cannot be verified remotely.

risks.risk: The battery is dead or unable to hold a charge.
risks.proof: A video clip of the fan running for at least 5 minutes while unplugged from the wall.
risks.if_unproven: as a standard corded AC fan with a dead battery.

risks.risk: The motor is burnt or the blades do not spin.
risks.proof: A video showing the fan powered on and blades spinning at multiple speeds.
risks.if_unproven: as scrap or for parts only.

risks.proof: A video showing the fan head rotating from side to side while running.

risks.risk: Missing remote control (often included with this model).
risks.proof: A photo of the remote control next to the fan.

proof_requests: Video of the fan operating at high speed while unplugged from the wall socket.
Video showing the oscillation function working.
Photo of the back of the fan or the base to see the battery compartment.
Photo of the remote control if available.
response.reason: The item is identified as a QASA standing fan. It can be priced at the worst-case value of a non-functional rechargeable unit (acting as a basic AC fan) until battery and motor health are proven.
